ENGINEERING MECHANICS STATICS
  Beams – External Effects
Shear, Bending, and Torsion

 In   addition   to   supporting   tension   or
compression,  a beam  can  resist  shear,
bending, and torsion. These three effects are
 illustrated in Fig. The force V is called the
shear  force,  the  couple M  is  called  the
bending moment, and the couple T is called
a torsional moment.These   effects   represent   the   vector
components of the resultant of the forces
acting on a transverse section of the beam
as shown in the lower part of the figure.
